name: Kiron Labs - Rob - LinkedIn Content Curation v1

parameters.content:
## Required credentials
- **DeepSeek API - Rob** (HTTP Header Auth, header `Authorization: Bearer <key>`)
- **Google Sheets - Rob** (OAuth2)
- **Telegram - Rob** (Bot Token)

## Environment variables (Settings > Variables or .env)
- `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID_ROB` — Rob's Telegram chat_id
- `DRY_RUN` — 'true' or 'false'. When 'true' the draft is generated but NOT logged to Sheets and NOT sent for real review (only a Telegram preview).

The spreadsheet ID is already embedded directly in the Google Sheets nodes.

## Before activating
1. Create the 'RSS-Sources' tab in the sheet (see note below) and load it with the initial sources.
2. Create the 'Rob-LinkedIn' tab in the sheet with the columns described in the note on the right.
3. Set up the Telegram bot and add the inline buttons (already included) for approve/discard.
4. This workflow NEVER auto-publishes to LinkedIn. It only prepares drafts for human review.
5. Also import 'Rob - RSS Sources Health Check v1' — it validates the URLs weekly and notifies you on Telegram if any breaks.

## Columns of the 'RSS-Sources' tab
- source_name
- url
- category (engineering_blog | em | ai_for_teams)
- active (TRUE/FALSE) — to add or remove a source without touching the workflow, just edit this column or delete/add the row
- last_checked
- last_status (ok | error: <detail>)

This main workflow only reads rows with active = TRUE. Automatic URL validation runs in the separate 'Rob - RSS Sources Health Check v1' workflow, which updates last_checked and last_status every week.

## Columns of the 'Rob-LinkedIn' tab
- date
- profile
- channel
- sources_consulted
- article_title
- article_url
- draft_content
- content_hash
- status  (pending review | approved for publishing | discarded | published)
- published_at
- telegram_message_id
- day_topic (the topic assigned that day according to the fixed M-F rotation, for traceability)

The status is updated automatically when Rob replies with the Telegram buttons (Approve / Discard). The actual LinkedIn publishing remains a manual step or a separate workflow — this workflow only prepares and logs the draft.

## Daily topic rotation (fixed, editable in the 'Code - Topic of the Day' node)
Monday: AI applied to team leadership
Tuesday: Developer Experience and productivity
Wednesday: Process improvement (Planning, Sprint, PR Reviews, onboarding)
Thursday: Practical Engineering Management with measurable results
Friday: Technology applied to real life in a light and pleasant way to close the work week

nodes.name: DeepSeek - Filter Relevant Articles

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'deepseek-chat', temperature: 0.2, response_format: { type: 'json_object' }, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: 'You are the LinkedIn content editor for Roberto Barcenas, an Engineering Manager actively looking for an EM or Head of Engineering role. Positioning: an EM who uses AI as an enabler to improve processes, develop teams and increase engineering productivity. AI is never the protagonist; the team and the working system are. Topics that YES: AI applied to team leadership, developer experience, process improvement such as planning, sprint, PR reviews, onboarding, practical engineering management with measurable results, sustainable backend and platforms, real cases with metrics. Topics that NO: model benchmarks, GPT vs Claude vs DeepSeek comparisons, prompts and prompting techniques, generic AI news without a leadership angle, generic corporate content. Today the priority topic of the day is: ' + $('Code - Topic of the Day').first().json.topic + '. Give preference to articles that connect with that topic even if they touch other angles of the positioning; if none connects well with the topic of the day, still select the most relevant ones for the overall positioning. You will receive a list of articles in JSON. Select at most 3 that best serve this positioning and discard the rest. Respond only with a JSON with this exact shape: { selected: [ { title: string, link: string, source: string, summary: string, reason: string } ] }. If none apply, respond { selected: [] }.' }, { role: 'user', content: JSON.stringify($json.articles) } ] }) }}
parameters.notes: Selects at most 3 articles aligned with the editorial line. Discards benchmarks, comparisons and generic AI news.

nodes.notes: Selects at most 3 articles aligned with the editorial line. Discards benchmarks, comparisons and generic AI news.

nodes.name: DeepSeek - Generate Post Draft

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'deepseek-chat', temperature: 0.6, response_format: { type: 'json_object' }, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: 'You write LinkedIn posts for Roberto Barcenas, an Engineering Manager looking for an EM or Head of Engineering role earning above 150000 MXN per month. Your voice is that of an informed curator, not someone who lived the story as the protagonist: you found an interesting article or topic and you share it with your take on why it matters for other Engineering Managers and engineering leaders. You must generate the draft in TWO languages: Spanish (ES) first and English (EN) after. Each version must read as a complete and natural post written by a native speaker of that language, not as a literal word-by-word translation, but telling the same content. Mandatory style in both languages: conversational and direct, like someone sharing something they found and found valuable, not like a neutral reporter nor like someone narrating a personal team experience they did not live. Short sentences, one idea per sentence or paragraph. Lots of visual space between blocks, little dense prose. Use first person ONLY to present the finding and your opinion about it, never to narrate an invented team story (avoid decidimos, empezamos, nos dimos cuenta, agregamos, and their English equivalents we decided, we started, we realized, we added, unless the original article literally describes an experience of Roberto, which is not the case). Instead use frames like: I found this article or topic, it seems relevant to me because, what caught my attention is, this connects with a problem I often see in engineering teams. Professional but natural language: Engineering Manager, Planning Poker, Story Points, PR, CI, QA, etc, when they are a real part of the content. It must not sound inspirational; the reason why the topic matters has to be supported by argument, not generic enthusiasm. Totally avoid phrases with this generic AI-written pattern, in any language: the problem was not X but Y, the problem is real, and here comes the interesting part, but that was not all, the real question is, and how do you do it, this changed the game, more than a tool it is, AI did not come to replace, it is not about X but about Y. Even if grammatically correct they do not sound natural, they sound engineered for engagement. The post must show: what you found (the concrete topic or finding of the article), why it seems relevant to you for an Engineering Manager or engineering leader (your opinion, with concrete argument, not empty enthusiasm), and data or metrics from the article if they exist, integrated into the explanation, not as a loose corporate KPI. This post is standalone; do not add continuity phrases toward previous or next posts. Emojis: use them as visual elements, at most one per important block, never as decoration nor in excess. Allowed set and meaning: rocket for start or launch, clipboard for process or tasks, bar chart for metrics or results, gear for engineering or technical process, robot for AI, lightning for impact or speed, joker for Planning Poker, link for repository or source. Sources: always include the source of the article or topic explicitly and separated from your opinion, marked with the book or link emoji before the link, making it clear that this is what you found and this is what you think about it. AI is never the protagonist of the content unless the article topic is literally about AI, and in that case it is treated as a tool within an engineering process, never as the protagonist of a personal story. Final rule: share what you found and why it matters to you, do not invent an experience you did not have, and do not tell the reader what to think, give your reasoning and let them draw their own conclusion. If a sentence sounds like it was written to sound good on LinkedIn instead of sharing a real finding with an honest opinion, remove it. Today the priority topic is: ' + $('Code - Topic of the Day').first().json.topic + '. Connect the draft with that angle whenever the article allows it, in both languages. Max 1100 characters per version (ES and EN counted separately). Respond only with a JSON with this exact shape: { draft_es: string, draft_en: string }.' }, { role: 'user', content: JSON.stringify({ title: $json.title, link: $json.link, source: $json.source, summary: $json.summary, reason: $json.reason }) } ] }) }}
parameters.notes: Runs once per selected article (at most 3).
